attributes.title: Level 6

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about using different combinations of symbols in your code to check and compare the values of multiple variables.

questions.hint: What does each symbol represent in JavaScript?
questions.title: [Match one per answer]  Match each operator symbol with its name:
questions.correctResponse: Remember, in blocks you would use <and> or <or> as Boolean operators; in JavaScript, you can use && or || as Boolean operators. A relational operator >= compares the value on either side of the operator.

questions.hint: What does the && symbol represent in JavaScript?
questions.title: [Select one] What condition(s) needs to be true, in order for the blizzard screen effect to start?

answers.text: The A button needs to be pressed.
The score needs to be greater than 5.
The A button needs to be pressed OR the score needs to be greater than 5.
The A button needs to be pressed AND the score needs to be greater than 5.

questions.correctResponse: When a Boolean AND operator (&&) is used, both conditions need to be true in order for the code to run.

questions.hint: What does each part of the relational operator >=  tell you?
questions.title: [Select all that apply] This relational operator >= checks if the value on the left is ___________ the value on the right.
questions.correctResponse: You might use this relational operator (>=) to check if a variable is greater than or equal to a certain value at different points in a project!

questions.title: [Open response] How might you use a Boolean operator in a project?
questions.correctResponse: Boolean operators can be used in lots of different ways! You might use them in a project to keep track of game events and cause something to happen if a certain (or multiple) condition(s) are true!

subgroups.title: Boolean and Relational Operators!
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about using different combinations of symbols in your code to check and compare the values of multiple variables.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 6 of Blue Belt! Before you create your final Blue Belt project, there are a few neat tricks to learn that could take your game to the next level! In this level, you’ll learn more about Boolean and relational operators, which can be used to check if 1 or more conditions are true in a project. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 6:

badges.title: Making Big Decisions
badges.description: Use Boolean and relational operators as part of conditional statements in JavaScript.

badges.title: Package Deal
badges.description: Use a Boolean AND operator in JavaScript.

badges.title: Hard Pressed
badges.description: Check if a button is pressed as part of a conditional statement.

badges.title: Comparatively Speaking
badges.description: Use a relational operator in JavaScript.

badges.title: Reassess the Situation
badges.description: Use an assignment operator to give an existing variable a new value.

badges.title: This or That
badges.description: Use a Boolean OR operator in JavaScript.
